note: Literature directly delineates BRD4-related phenotypes across fetal, pediatric, and adult stages, supporting age-dependent evaluation.

evidence.text: Jouret et al. assembled an international cohort of 14 patients including fetuses, children, and adults to delineate dysmorphic features at different ages and establish recognizable clinical patterns across age stages.

source.title: Understanding the new BRD4‐related syndrome: Clinical and genomic delineation with an international cohort study
source.quote: We formed an international collaborative study, and collected 14 new patients, including two fetuses. We performed phenotype and genotype analysis, integrated prenatal findings from fetopathological examinations, phenotypes of pediatric patients and adults. We report the first cohort of patients with BRD4-related disorder and delineate the dysmorphic features at different ages.
